text:
alice: Heads up — hitting a weird auth behavior in py SDK when rotating API keys for long-lived AsyncClient instances.
ben: Can you paste a minimal repro?
alice: Yep. flow: create AsyncClient(key=A), start background tasks, rotate env var/key to B, new requests still use A until process restart.
carlos: That's expected if the client caches the auth header at init. But we should expose a credential provider callback.
alice: Agreed. Current workaround is to recreate clients on rotation or restart service, which is rough for serverless/worker pools.
ben: Does the blocking Client behave the same?
alice: I tested sync client briefly — it picks up new key when we call Client.close() and re-init, but still doesn't hot-swap automatically. Async client seems to hold reference to _api_key string on creation.
emily: SDK-bot: @alice filed issue #1724 (py-sdk): async-client retains API key after env rotation — link https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1724 :eyes:
ben: Can we implement a CredentialsProvider interface? signature like: async def get_api_key() -> str / or sync call allowed.
carlos: Proposal: accept either api_key str OR api_key_provider: Callable[[], Union[str, Awaitable[str]]]. SDK resolves before each request. Also add optional caching TTL.
alice: That would be perfect. Also need to ensure typing plays nicely with AsyncClient and callables in typing stubs. Current typeshed uses Optional[str] for api_key only.
ben: PR idea: add parameter api_key_provider: Optional[Callable[[], Union[str, Awaitable[str]]]] = None and deprecate hot-swapping env hacks. Keep backward compat: if api_key_provider is None and api_key is provided, behave as today.
emily: UX question: should we auto-fallback to environment variables when provider returns None? That could be surprising.
carlos: I'd prefer explicit: provider returns None => raise AuthError. env var fallback only if no provider and no explicit api_key param. Document precedence: explicit api_key > api_key_provider > env var > config file.
alice: Repro logs: 
```
INFO Starting worker pool
DEBUG Using api key from client: a_sk_live_123
... (rotate env to b_sk_live_456) ...
DEBUG Sending request with api key: a_sk_live_123
```
No reauth attempt.
ben: Another bug: when provider is async and raises CancelledError, request hangs. Need request-level timeout and wrap provider call.
emily: Good catch. Also add examples in quickstart and sample-app showing how to use async provider with vault/kms.
carlos: I'll draft the PR with types and tests. Plan: add unit tests for sync provider, async provider, provider raising error, provider returning None, and TTL behavior.
alice: Thanks! For now, I added a small wrapper in our service to call client.set_api_key(await provider()) when rotation webhook hits. Ugly but works.
ben: Recording feature request: add api_key_provider + ttl + provider_timeout + clear precedence docs.
emily: I'll update quickstart snippets and add an example file in examples/async-rotation.py.
carlos: Assigning issue to myself, will post PR link when ready.
alice: Appreciate it. One more ask — can we log masked fingerprint of the active key for easier debugging (like first 6 chars)?
ben: Good idea. We'll add masked_key in debug logs: a_sk_l*****.
sdk-bot: Reminder: new PRs should include changelog entry and migration notes.
alice: OK thanks — will watch the issue. :thumbsup:
